title_ar: الشيخ الددو: من واجبات المسلم اختيار الأكفأ والأصلح
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew: Among the Muslim's Obligations Is to Choose the Most Competent and the Most Fitting
body_ar:
قال فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو إن من واجبات المسلم أن يختار للتمثيل الأفضل والأكفأ والأصلح لدين الله؛ الذي تقوم به الحجة لله، فذلك من الأمانة التي وضعها الله في عنق الإنسان ومن التعاون على البر والتقوى الذي أمر الله به.

فعلى المسلم أن يعلم وهو يتوجه إلى صناديق الاقتراع أنه سيسأل بين يدي الله عن اختياره السياسي؛ وتصويته لمن لا يستحق.

ووجه الشيخ الددو النصيحة للمسلمين؛ خلال خطبة الجمعة بجامع مركز تكوين العلماء اليوم 08/11/2013 سواء المترشح منهم أو الناخب؛ مطالبا الجميع في هذا الموسم السياسي بالانتباه لخطر الكلام وضرره؛ وحرمة أعراض المسلمين وعن الذم والشم فيما لا وجه فيه شرعا؛ منبها المسلمين إلى التعفف عن اللغو فهو لا خير فيه.

وأضاف فضيلة الشيخ أن التنافس يجب أن يكون نزيها وفي الخير؛ أما التنافس في التسلط على أموال الضعفاء والفقراء فهو تنافس في الشر وفي جراثيم جهنم، ومن الجسارة على الله؛ فعلى المتنافسين أن يأخذوا الحذر لأنفسهم من الآن.

وأكد الشيخ أن على الجميع أن يراجع نيته ويصدق مع الله ويحذر من التبذير والحرام، فمن أراد النجاح فعليه أن يعلم أنه من عند الله.
body_en:
His eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew said that among the obligations (wājibāt) of the Muslim is that he choose for [political] representation the best, the most competent and the most fitting for the religion of God — the one through whom the case is established before God. That is part of the trust (amānah) which God has placed upon the neck of man, and part of the mutual assistance in righteousness and God-consciousness (taqwā) that God has commanded.

So the Muslim must know, as he goes to the ballot boxes, that he will be questioned before God about his political choice, and about his voting for one who does not deserve it.

Sheikh al-Dedew directed this counsel to the Muslims during the Friday sermon (khuṭbah) at the congregational mosque of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars today, 08/11/2013, to candidate and voter alike; calling upon everyone in this political season to be alert to the danger of speech and its harm, and to the inviolability of the honour of the Muslims, and [warning them] against disparagement and abuse where there is no warrant for it in the Sharia; and alerting the Muslims to abstain from idle talk, for there is no good in it.

His eminence the Sheikh added that competition must be honourable and in what is good; but as for competing to gain control over the wealth of the weak and the poor, that is a competition in evil and in the germs of Hellfire, and an act of temerity towards God. So those who compete should take heed for themselves from now.

The Sheikh affirmed that everyone must re-examine his intention (niyyah), be truthful with God, and beware of wasteful spending and of what is forbidden (ḥarām); and that whoever desires success should know that it comes from God.

flags.arabic: صيغة الخبر الصحفي (قال فضيلة الشيخ... مؤكدا... وأضاف...)
options: render as a site news report, with the Sheikh's words marked as the site's paraphrase
render as a text by the Sheikh
flags.note: NOT A TEXT BY THE SHEIKH. This record is the site's own news write-up. Outside the passages placed in quotation marks, every formulation is the site editor's indirect report of what the Sheikh said, not his own wording, and the English preserves the reporting verbs (the Sheikh said that..., he affirmed that...) so that a reader can see this. It must not be displayed as a fatwa or as a text of his. The underlying address or lecture is not in this record.

flags.context: the list of things the Sheikh warned against in the election season
options: against disparagement and abuse (reading الشم as الشتم)
reproduce the source's word and leave the lacuna visible
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT (house rule 11). الشم as printed means 'smelling' and is meaningless in this list. The evident word is الشتم, 'reviling, abuse', with a dropped tāʾ; it pairs naturally with الذم. Translated by the evident sense and flagged; body_ar preserves the source. Not restored silently.

flags.arabic: فهو تنافس في الشر وفي جراثيم جهنم
flags.context: the Sheikh's warning to those competing for office
options: a competition in evil and in the germs of Hellfire
a competition in evil and in the seeds of Hellfire
a competition in evil and in the breeding-grounds of Hellfire
flags.note: جراثيم جهنم is an unusual image and is not a glossary term. جرثومة is literally a root, stock or seed-bed, and in later usage a germ or microbe; the plural here is doing rhetorical rather than technical work, and the referent may be an allusion to a report the site does not name. Rendered literally, with alternatives, rather than smoothed into a paraphrase. Note that this is the site's report of his words, not his own text.

flags.arabic: أن يختار للتمثيل الأفضل والأكفأ والأصلح لدين الله
flags.context: the opening ruling of the report, delivered in an election season
options: a duty about how one chooses, stated in general terms
an endorsement of electoral participation as such
an instruction to vote for a particular tendency
flags.note: EDITORIAL. The Arabic states a duty about HOW one chooses, in general terms; it names no party and no candidate, and the word in the reporter's summary is واجبات, 'obligations', not a formal fatwa. Read in English, detached from the Mauritanian November 2013 election it was preached in, it can easily be quoted as the Sheikh directing Muslims how to vote, including in jurisdictions where clerical direction of voting is itself contentious. Translated faithfully and flagged; the site must not caption it as election guidance.

translator_notes: التمثيل here is political representation (the context is candidacy and the ballot box); '[political]' is supplied in brackets as a marked expansion, per style guide section 1.
تقوم به الحجة لله is rendered 'through whom the case is established before God', in the legal-theory sense of ḥujjah (a proof that binds), not 'argument' in the everyday sense.

يجب أن يكون نزيها is the reporter's 'must be honourable'. It is a report of exhortation, not a formal ruling, so it has not been given the fixed 'obligatory (wājib)' rendering; the one place the noun واجبات appears it is rendered 'obligations (wājibāt)'.
التبذير is 'wasteful spending' (Qur'anic tabdhīr), not 'extravagance' in the neutral sense.
